transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-02-06 14:30 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mike Chen (CTO - Quantashift), Sarah Lopez (ML Eng), Evan Park (SRE)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
- Quick runthrough of last week's bench results. Redwood showed lower p50 but p99 still close to incumbent in some long-tail cases.
- Discussed routing policies, KV/prefix cache gains, quantization tradeoffs.
- Next steps: share detailed CSV, confirm traffic profile, and agree on whether to request dedicated slots for peak traffic.

Topics: latency deltas, throughput headroom, unit cost per token, dedicated vs hosted routing, security integration (KMS/SSO), fallback playbook

Action items (verbatim above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey, good afternoon everyone, thanks for making time. quick roll call?
[00:05] Mike: mike here, sarah, evan — all good on our side.
[00:08] Sarah: yep, thanks. we tuned the load generator overnight per priya's notes.
[00:12] Priya: perfect, i'll start by walking through the key numbers. so we ran three model configs: baseline (incumbent), redwood-hosted-quant (int8-ish), and redwood-routing-with-kvcache.
[00:22] Priya: p50 latency baseline is ~85ms; redwood-hosted p50 came in at 62ms — so about 27ms delta.
[00:29] Sarah: ok that's promising, what's p95 and p99 look like?
[00:32] Priya: p95 baseline 210ms, redwood 180ms; p99 baseline 430, redwood 390. so long tail improved but still close in some tail scenarios.
[00:40] Evan: those p99s, were they with cold kv cache or after warmup?
[00:43] Priya: mixed; we did an 8k token warmup for steady-state runs and also ran cold-start batches. the p99 gap tighter on cold starts — likely serialization and routing hop overhead when fallback occurs.
[00:51] Alex: just to add, our routing was letting requests go to cheaper regional variants during burst mode which added an extra hop. we can disable cross-region fallback for your pilot if you want to reduce p99 at the expense of cost.
[01:02] Mike: can you quantify the cost delta? even a 10% latency gain might blow our cost target.
[01:06] Alex: sure — rough ballpark from test: enabling dedicated regional routing pushed unit cost up about 18% on these workloads because we couldn't do prefix K/V reuse across regions as effectively. i'll put exact numbers in the CSV.
[01:15] Sarah: what about throughput? we saw baseline saturates at ~420 rps on our infra; your hosted runs hit 560 rps before tail latency jumps. is that right?
[01:23] Priya: yes, on continuous batching the throughput headroom was +30% in a steady stream workload. at bursty small requests throughput benefits shrink because batching can't fill.
[01:32] Sarah: can you remind us about batching window config? we wanted conservative latency (<=200ms p95) and still want batching to help.
[01:38] Priya: current batching window was 12ms with adaptive expand; we can drop to 6ms to favor latency, but throughput will dip ~8-10% at high QPS.
[01:45] Mike: hmm. for our use case, most queries are short — 16 to 64 tokens — so maybe smaller window is fine. but we need p95 under 200ms always.
[01:54] Alex: ok noted. one other place we saw p99 regressions: token-level KV cache misses for dialogs with long context — your traffic included a subset of long-chats. if we enable lite-prefix caching and increase kv cache retention we can cut tail by another 30-40ms.
[02:06] Evan: does that require model changes or infra only?
[02:09] Priya: infra only — runtime config. we'll share the exact flags. priya: (laughs) sorry, that was me repeating.
[02:14] Sarah: what's the impact on memory? quantized model runs + boosted KV retention might bump GPU mem by ~6–8GB?
[02:20] Priya: roughly, yes. for some of the medium-size GPUs we tested we had to reduce batch max tokens from 1024 to 768 to fit. for your fleet we should map to instance types we recommended last week.
[02:30] Mike: security question — our security folks asked whether KMS integrates with your private deployment; they saw SOC2 but want to know about customer-managed keys.
[02:36] Alex: yes, for private we offer customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. hosted can do envelope encryption with CMK in a partner KMS; we'll send the architecture doc.
[02:44] Mike: and SSO? SAML / SCIM for role sync?
[02:47] Alex: supported. we also provide token-level RBAC in the console.
[02:51] Evan: is audit logging preserved across fallbacks (i.e., if request is routed to fallback model, do logs still show original routing decision)?
[02:56] Priya: yes, we attach metadata with routing trace id — shows model variant, region, and fallback reason. logs are retained per tenant. retention window depends on plan; we'll include that in the security packet.
[03:06] Sarah: could you walk us through the one-to-one comparison vs the incumbent for the peak hour we shared last week? that's the thing — baseline vendor had custom caching on edge and they were beating you on certain short-lived spikes.
[03:18] Priya: for the peak hour case, incumbent had slightly better headroom on sub-200ms short queries because they have a closer edge cache and fewer serialization steps. however, once you look at unit cost per million queries, Redwood had 12% lower unit cost in steady-state and similar or better p50. so it's a trade.
[03:34] Mike: ok, so if we prioritize latency for peak 15-minute windows we might need dedicated slots?
[03:38] Alex: yes, dedicated capacity for the peak window will virtually eliminate cross-tenant interference and give you guaranteed throughput — at a reserved cost. we can model a burst carve-out so you're not paying reserved 24/7 for occasional peaks.
[03:47] Evan: how quickly can dedicated slots be spun up? we don't want a multi-week lead time.
[03:51] Alex: depends on capacity but for your region we can do a 7–10 day provisioning timeline once contract is in. for pilot reasons we can do a temporary slot reservation for testing within 48 hours if we pre-approve.
[04:01] Sarah: are there any regression alerts or eval hooks? we'd like automatic quality monitoring when we change quantization.
[04:06] Priya: yep, Redwood Optimize can run a continuous eval against your golden prompt set and alert on automatic quality regressions. we can add that to pilot for a short window.
[04:14] Mike: great. on the costing — can you give an example of per-token cost vs incumbent for a typical 32-token response?
[04:21] Alex: i'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet but ballpark: incumbent $X.XX per 1k tokens, Redwood hosted $~0.88 of that for int8 variants; dedicated slot reduces per-token marginal cost further under sustained throughput.
[04:33] Sarah: one odd thing we noticed — during one run the redwood p95 spiked to 480ms briefly and logs showed a region timeout then reroute. is there a way to avoid cross-region reroutes for critical paths?
[04:44] Priya: yes we can pin routing policies by tag/route and set strict SLO-based routing to never fallback cross-region for your production route. for pilot we used a permissive policy, that caused reroutes under transient infra blips.
[04:55] Evan: what's the debug story? how do we correlate a request id to the model execution trace?
[04:59] Priya: every request gets a trace id; we include a link to the execution traces and token timings in the console and in the audit log entry. we'll share sample links.
[05:08] Mike: perfect. any blockers from our side?
[05:11] Alex: just we need your 48h traffic histogram and confirmation of whether peak needs hard p95 <200ms or softer target.
[05:18] Mike: we'll get that to you by Tuesday.
[05:20] Sarah: last quick Q — is there any change for GDPR / data residency if we route to different regions?
[05:26] Alex: yes, routing across regions can have residency implications; if you need EU-only we can enforce region-bound routing. we'll also include data-at-rest encryption notes and retention windows in the packet.
[05:36] Mike: ok good. wondering about the final step — do we want a short lab run where we force a peak 15-minute window and watch behavior?
[05:43] Alex: i'd recommend that. Priya can run that with you this week: simulate peak with your real histogram and we'll run both permissive and pinned routing so you can compare.
[05:52] Priya: i'll schedule the lab and post playbook steps.
[05:55] Evan: timeline?
[05:56] Priya: Planning for Wednesday/Thursday — i'll email a calendar invite after this call.
[06:01] Alex: great. quick recap: priya will post config snippets and run the KV cache walkthrough; alex sends costing csv and dedicated/reserved slot delta; quantashift shares traffic histogram; schedule peak simulation lab. anyone disagree?
[06:13] Mike: sounds right. thanks all.
[06:15] Sarah: thanks, talk soon.
[06:18] Alex: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
